improvement_relation.basis: The CLI now leaves branch unset when the caller omitted --branch, allowing Environment claim acquisition to refresh and verify the live registered checkout before resolving branch identity. Regression tests exercise that exact CLI path while retaining strict validation for explicit branch values.

outcome.implementation_change: cmd_claims no longer copies an entry-time branch into a worktree scope when --branch was omitted. An explicitly supplied branch remains an exact precondition checked against the live registered checkout after claim acquisition refresh.
outcome.interpretation_limit: The regression verifies the stale-precondition path and preserves exact checkout verification. It does not establish a reduction in real-world intervention frequency, time, or tool calls.
outcome.verified_change: The claim CLI regression now changes a registered checkout branch after session selection, omits --branch, and acquires a claim on the live branch through ordinary claim acquisition without an explicit reconcile. Explicit branch and unselected worktree cases are also covered.

pressure_hypothesis.actionable_recommendation: Leave branch unspecified when the caller omitted --branch. Let claim acquisition refresh and verify the exact registered checkout, then derive its current branch. Continue treating an explicit --branch as an exact live precondition.
pressure_hypothesis.basis: A real claim attempt after a registered checkout branch change failed with working-checkout-unavailable because the CLI had included an entry-time branch in the exact worktree scope. The same campaign later succeeded after explicit session reconciliation. Source inspection showed that cmd_claims copied the selected-checkout branch whenever --branch was omitted.
